_comment_intro: ArtScope painting config. Copy to painting.json and fill in. Every field below is consumed by at least one page. Delete _comment fields once you've read them or keep them for reference; the runtime ignores any key starting with _.
_comment_id: slug used as the base name for the DZI tile pyramid and a few asset filenames. No spaces.
_comment_site: Shown in the nav top-left and footer. The tagline appears as the brand subtitle on every page.

painting.title: English / conventional title
painting._comment_dates: Both are strings to allow date ranges, circa values, etc. e.g. 'c. 1503'.
painting._comment_dims: [width_cm, height_cm]. Used in the meta bar.
painting.current_state: Freeform note on condition / restoration history.

scan._comment_url: Tile pyramid manifest, generated by scripts/make_tiles.py. Use this for the gigapixel-smooth explorer experience.
scan._comment_fallback: Single-image fallback. Used if DZI fails to load and as the source for build_assets.py and run_analysis.py.
scan._comment_dims: Actual pixel dimensions of the scan referenced by url/fallback_url. Drives the SVG overlay aspect ratio and the source-pixel readout in the lab.
scan.source: Where the scan came from (museum, Wikimedia, etc.). Used in the analysis citation.
scan._comment_ref: Optional: link to the highest-resolution gigapixel scan even if you're not hosting it. Shown in the analysis sources section.

_comment_motif: The portrait-orientation hero crop. Iconic figure or detail. Used on the system bonus page and as fallback hero.
_comment_caption: Short tag shown under the motif. Useful for noting position or significance.
_comment_hero: Wide landscape atmosphere strip. Used as faded background on the system page hero.

design_principles.note: If true, renders a 'design principles' section on the system page. Disabled by default; leave false unless you have something to say there.

measurements._comment: These are surfaced on the analysis page section 04 as the measured-values block. Populate from scripts/run_analysis.py output.

extraction_method.name: HSV-filtered region sampling
steps: Convert RGB to HSV in normalized [0,1] space
Define rectangular regions over known pigment patches
For each region, filter by hue range and a minimum value threshold
Take top 70% by saturation, return their channel-wise median
Names assigned manually with reference to the historical pigment
extraction_method._comment: Rendered as the numbered methodology pipeline on the system page. Free to rewrite for your painting's pigment story.

pigments.name: Placeholder Pigment 1
pigments._comment_region: [x0, y0, x1, y1] as 0..1 fractions of the source image. Defines the rectangle to sample this pigment from.
pigments._comment_hue: Optional [low, high] in 0..1 to filter pixels by hue. Use null for unfiltered. For ranges crossing red (e.g. wine, vermillion), use [0.95, 0.06] which means hue >= 0.95 OR hue <= 0.06.
pigments.historical: historical pigment identity (lead white, ultramarine, vermillion, etc.)

the lab and system pages render the palette as a 4-column grid; 12 fits cleanly. Fewer works but the layout will look sparse. More breaks the grid.

hotspots._comment_id: slug used as the URL hash anchor + thumbnail filename (assets/hotspots/<id>.jpg). Hyphenated lowercase.
hotspots.name: Main subject
hotspots._comment_region: [x0, y0, x1, y1] as 0..1 fractions of the source. The explorer flies here when clicked; the lab samples this rectangle.
hotspots.summary: 1-3 sentence prose. Shown in the explorer sidebar when this hotspot is active.

the lab uses these as quick-select buttons. The explorer renders them as click-targets over the painting plus cards in the sidebar.
